1: # opencode-container
2: 
3: Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.
4: 
5: ## Quickstart
6: 
7: **Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).
8: 
9: ```bash
10: make build
11: make serve
12: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
13: ```
14: 
15: That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
16: 
17: ## Containers
18: 
19: | Container | Dockerfile | Mode | Port | Profiles | Volumes | Purpose |
20: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
21: | `opencode-serve` | `serve.dockerfile` | `serve` | 4096 | — | data, config | Headless HTTP server: web UI + REST API + OpenAPI doc. Starts with an initialized git project. |
22: | `opencode-web` | `web.dockerfile` | `web` | 4098 | — | data, config | Same as `serve` but uses `opencode web` (auto-instantiates a project on first load). |
23: | `opencode-acp` | `acp.dockerfile` | `acp` | 4097 | — | — | ACP (Agent Client Protocol) JSON-RPC server over stdio, bridged to TCP via `socat`. For ACP-compatible clients (Cline, continue.dev). |
24: | `opencode-issue-processor` | `issue-processor.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Batch: iterates all open issues from configured repos, pipes each into `opencode run`. Exits when done. |
25: | `opencode-plan-issue` | `plan-issue.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | One-shot: clones a repo, analyzes a specific issue, posts an implementation plan as a GitHub comment. Exits when done. |
26: | `opencode-generic-worker` | `generic-worker.dockerfile` | `run` | — | `manual` | data, config | Clone a repo, bootstrap opencode config from a mounted volume, execute a mounted script or inline command. |
27: 
28: ### Which container do I pick?
29: 
30: | You want to... | Use |
31: |---|---|
32: | Run a headless OpenCode server with a web UI | `opencode-serve` (`make serve`) |
33: | Run OpenCode web with an auto-created project | `opencode-web` (`make web`) |
34: | Connect an ACP client (e.g. Cline, continue.dev) | `opencode-acp` (`make acp`) |
35: | Process all open issues from one or more repos | `opencode-issue-processor` (`make process`) |
36: | Analyze a single issue and post a plan | `opencode-plan-issue` (`make plan`) |
37: | Run a custom script inside a cloned repo | `opencode-generic-worker` (`make generic`) |
38: | Run a continuous issue-resolution workflow | `workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh` |
39: | Pass `--help` flags to opencode | `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` |
40: 
41: ### Managing repos for the issue processor
42: 
43: The issue processor (`process-issues.sh`) hardcodes target repositories:
44: 
45: ```bash
46: REPOS=(
47:   "tbrandenburg/made"
48:   "tbrandenburg/pyrag"
49: )
50: ```
51: 
52: Edit this array in `process-issues.sh` to change which repos it scans for open issues. Each entry is an `owner/repo` pair understood by `gh issue list`.
53: 
54: ## Architecture
55: 
56: ### Why this design?
57: 
58: OpenCode supports three runtime modes — `serve` (HTTP API), `web` (HTTP + instant project), and `acp` (JSON-RPC over stdio) — plus a `run` mode for one-off agent invocations. Each mode has different network and lifecycle requirements. Rather than crafting a single monolithic image, each mode gets its own Dockerfile. This gives us:
59: 
60: - **Isolation by purpose**: A `socat` dependency for ACP doesn't bloat the serve image. Git and `gh` CLI for runners don't affect the server image.
61: - **Independent lifecycle**: Serve/web containers run long-term. Runner containers (issue-processor, plan-issue, generic-worker) are ephemeral — they clone, execute, and exit.
62: - **Clean `--help` passthrough**: Serve/web use `ENTRYPOINT` so `docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help` works naturally. Runner containers use `CMD`/`ENTRYPOINT` pointing to their shell scripts.
63: 
64: #### serve vs web — what's the difference?
65: 
66: Both `opencode-serve` and `opencode-web` run HTTP servers. The difference:
67: 
68: - **`serve`** (`opencode serve`): Requires an existing git-initialized project. The Dockerfile creates one at build time (`git init` + commit). Good for teams that want to control the project lifecycle.
69: - **`web`** (`opencode web`): Auto-instantiates a project on first load. Slightly more self-service for new users.
70: 
71: Pick `serve` for production/team setups where you mount your own project. Pick `web` for quick experiments.
72: 
73: #### Why socat for ACP?
74: 
75: OpenCode's ACP mode speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over **stdin/stdout** — it's designed for local processes, not network sockets. To make it accessible inside Docker without modifying OpenCode itself, `socat` bridges a TCP listener to the process's stdio:
76: 
77: ```
78: TCP client → socat TCP-LISTEN:4097 → EXEC:"opencode acp" (stdin/stdout)
79: ```
80: 
81: This is a classic Unix pattern: a small, trusted tool adapts a stdio protocol to the network. It works on any port, requires zero OpenCode changes, and the container is completely transparent about it.
82: 
83: #### Why the profile/manual pattern?
84: 
85: ```yaml
86: profiles:
87:   - manual
88: ```
89: 
90: Containers with `profiles: [manual]` are excluded from `docker compose up` and `make run`. They must be launched explicitly:
91: 
92: ```bash
93: docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue
94: ```
95: 
96: This guarantees that ephemeral batch containers never accidentally stay running.
97: 
98: #### Why volume sharing?
99: 
100: All persistent containers share two named Docker volumes:
101: 
102: | Volume | Mount point | Contents |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | `opencode-data` | `/root/.local/share/opencode` | Session data, project history, LLM conversation logs |
105: | `opencode-config` | `/root/.config/opencode` | Global opencode config, agent definitions, custom prompts |
106: 
107: This means:
108: - Data survives container restarts and rebuilds
109: - Server and runner containers share the same config and history
110: - Volumes are created automatically by `docker compose up`
111: 
112: ### The workflows pattern
113: 
114: The `workflows/` directory contains reusable OpenCode workflow harnesses — shell scripts that orchestrate multi-step agent tasks in a structured, logged fashion. Each workflow:
115: 
116: 1. Clones or assumes a repository working copy
117: 2. Runs a sequence of steps (bash commands and/or `opencode` agent invocations)
118: 3. Logs everything to a dedicated log file with ISO-8601 timestamps
119: 4. Supports `--dry-run` for previewing without side effects
120: 
121: The main workflow:
122: - **`workflows/issue-resolution/.harness/continuous-issue-resolution.sh`**: A full issue lifecycle workflow — checks for open issues, syncs main, fixes via agent, commits/pushes, resolves CI errors, reviews the PR, raises follow-up issues, and merges. Intended to run inside the `generic-worker` container.
123: 
124: Workflow harness scripts implement these functions:
125: - `log()` — ISO-8601 UTC timestamped logging to stderr + log file
126: - `run_step()` — execute a bash function step with failure handling, output streaming via `tee`
127: - `run_agent()` — pipe a prompt to `opencode run --format json` with optional `--agent` selector
128: - `catch()` — centralized failure hook that logs the step name and exit code
129: 
130: ### Shell script robustness
131: 
132: Every `.sh` file in the repo root uses `set -euo pipefail` and validates required environment variables with descriptive error messages before proceeding. Shell scripts pass `shellcheck` at warning level with zero errors.
133: 
134: ### Base image
135: 
136: All containers use `node:22-slim` with:
137: - `opencode-ai` npm package installed globally (`npm install -g opencode-ai@latest`)
138: - `gh` CLI installed from GitHub releases tarball (runner containers only)
139: - `git`, `ca-certificates` for clone operations
140: - `socat` for the ACP bridge container
141: 
142: ### Network ports
143: 
144: ### Network isolation
145: 
146: Docker Compose creates a default bridge network (`opencode-container_default`). All containers within `docker-compose.yml` are on this network and can reach each other by service name (e.g., `http://opencode-serve:4096` from another container).
147: 
148: | Container | Host port | Container port | Protocol | Network | Auth |
149: |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
150: | `opencode-serve` | 4096 | 4096 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
151: | `opencode-web` | 4098 | 4098 | HTTP | bridge (default) | Basic auth via `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` |
152: | `opencode-acp` | 4097 | 4097 | TCP (JSON-RPC) | bridge (default) | None (stdio → TCP via socat) |
153: 
154: Runner containers (`manual` profile) have no published ports but are reachable by service name on the same network for outbound connections.
155: 
156: ## Environment Variables
157: 
158: | Variable | Affected containers | Required | Default | Security note |
159: |---|---|---|---|---|
160: | `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` | `opencode-serve`, `opencode-web` | no | `changeme` | HTTP Basic auth password. Override in docker-compose.yml or via `-e`. |
161: | `GH_TOKEN` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker`, workflow harnesses | yes (for GitHub operations) | — | GitHub personal access token. Pass via `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` at runtime. Never hardcoded in any Dockerfile or script — only interpolated by the calling shell. Never enters agent context. |
162: | `ISSUE_URL` | `plan-issue` | yes | — | Full GitHub issue URL, e.g. `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/42`. The script parses owner/repo/number from this URL. |
163: | `REPO_URL` | `generic-worker` | yes | — | Git clone URL. The generic worker validates this is non-empty before proceeding. |
164: | `ISSUE` | `generic-worker` | no | empty | Issue number passed as an environment variable to the child command or script. |
165: | `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/opencode-config` | Source directory (inside container) to copy config from when bootstrapping. Mount a host config directory here to inject custom agents. |
166: | `WORK_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/repo` | Destination directory for `git clone`. |
167: | `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` | `generic-worker` | no | `/root/.config/opencode` | Target directory for bootstrapped opencode global config. |
168: | `TARGETARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | no (build ARG) | `amd64` | Docker build `--build-arg` for architecture-specific `gh` CLI download. Set `--build-arg TARGETARCH=arm64` on ARM hosts. |
169: | `ARCH` | `issue-processor`, `plan-issue`, `generic-worker` | — | — | Internal variable derived from `TARGETARCH` in Dockerfile RUN commands. Not user-configurable. |
170: | `FLOWSH_LOG_DIR` | Test harness scripts (`tests/generic-worker/.harness/*.sh`) | no | `.flowsh/logs` | Override the log directory for generated flowsh harness scripts. Only relevant when developing or debugging test harnesses. |
171: 
172: ### Env var security rules
173: 
174: - `GH_TOKEN` is **never hardcoded** in any Dockerfile or `.sh` file. It is passed at container runtime from the calling shell's `gh auth token` output.
175: - `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` has a default value of `changeme` in both Dockerfiles and `docker-compose.yml`. Change it in production.
176: 
177: ## Commands
178: 
179: | Command | Description |
180: |---|---|
181: | `make install` | No-op (containers are self-contained). Prints informational message. |
182: | `make build` | `docker compose build` — builds all container images. |
183: | `make run` | `docker compose up -d` — starts all server containers in background. |
184: | `make stop` | `docker compose down` — stops all containers. |
185: | `make serve` | `docker compose up -d opencode-serve` — start only the headless server. |
186: | `make web` | `docker compose up -d opencode-web` — start only the web UI server. |
187: | `make acp` | `docker compose up -d opencode-acp` — start only the ACP bridge. |
188: | `make logs` | `docker compose logs -f` — follow logs from all running containers. |
189: | `make clean` | `docker compose down --remove-orphans -v` — stop and remove all containers, networks, and volumes. |
190: | `make process` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-issue-processor` — run the issue processor (exit when done). |
191: | `make plan` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-plan-issue` — run the issue planner (exit when done). |
192: | `make generic` | `docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker` — run the generic worker (exit when done). |
193: | `make lint` | `shellcheck` on all shell scripts (root + tests). |
194: | `make test` | Build + shellcheck + integration tests for all containers. |
195: | `make verify-quickstart` | Automated quickstart verification: build, serve, health-check, cleanup. |
196: | `make test-generic-worker` | Extended generic-worker integration tests (agent harness + repo inspection). |
197: 
198: ### --help passthrough
199: 
200: Because the serve/web containers use the pattern `ENTRYPOINT ["opencode", "serve|web"]` with `CMD` for flags, you can pass `--help` directly:
201: 
202: ```bash
203: docker compose run --rm opencode-serve --help
204: docker compose run --rm opencode-web --help
205: ```
206: 
207: ## Usage
208: 
209: ### Server containers (long-running)
210: 
211: ```bash
212: # Build everything
213: make build
214: 
215: # Start all servers
216: make run
217: 
218: # Start individual server
219: docker compose up -d opencode-serve
220: 
221: # Health check
222: curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
223: 
224: # View logs
225: make logs
226: 
227: # Stop everything
228: make stop
229: ```
230: 
231: ### Issue processor (batch, then exit)
232: 
233: ```bash
234: GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) make process
235: ```
236: 
237: The processor (`process-issues.sh`) iterates all open issues from hardcoded repos, piping each issue number into `opencode run`. Configure which repos to scan by editing `process-issues.sh`.
238: 
239: ### Issue planner (one-shot, then exit)
240: 
241: ```bash
242: ISSUE_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/30 \
243:   GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token) \
244:   make plan
245: ```
246: 
247: The planner (`plan-issue.sh`) parses the issue URL to extract owner/repo/number, clones the repo, then pipes a prompt into `opencode run` instructing it to read the issue, understand the codebase, and post a plan as a GitHub comment.
248: 
249: ### Generic worker (one-shot, clone + exec)
250: 
251: ```bash
252: # Mount a local script and execute it in the cloned repo:
253: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
254:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
255:   -e ISSUE=42 \
256:   -v ./workflows/issue-resolution/.opencode:/opencode-config:ro \
257:   -v ./my-script.sh:/script.sh:ro \
258:   /script.sh

260: # Pass an inline command instead:
261: docker compose run --rm opencode-generic-worker \
262:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \
263:   -e ISSUE=42 \

268: 1. Validates `REPO_URL` is set
269: 2. Clones the repo to `WORK_DIR` (default `/repo`)
270: 3. If `/opencode-config` exists (from a mounted volume), copies it to `OPENCODE_GLOBAL_DIR` to bootstrap custom agent definitions

273: 
274: **Security**: `GH_TOKEN`, `ISSUE_URL`, `REPO_URL`, and `ISSUE` are passed from the host environment and never read into agent context.

318:

331:   -e REPO_URL=https://github.com/owner/repo.git \

Docker images for running [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) — an AI coding agent — in every supported mode: HTTP server, web UI, ACP protocol bridge, and ephemeral issue-processing workers.

## Quickstart

**Prerequisites**: [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) (with Compose v2), [gh CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (for runner containers).

```bash
make build
make serve
curl -u "opencode:changeme" http://localhost:4096/global/health
```

That's it. Three commands, zero edits, and you have a running OpenCode server.
